output.summary: The deterministic verdict is FAIL. Both windows fail the latency rule: response_time_p95_ms observed 227ms against a 200ms threshold in the reference window (window-policy-summary 52367a66...: verdict FAIL, business_verdict FAIL, resource_verdict PASS) and in workload-01 (window-policy-summary 32c4c0c3...: verdict FAIL, business_verdict FAIL, resource_verdict PASS). All resource checks PASS (system-cpu-work ~0.15 vs compute-limit threshold 0.9; system-db-work ~0.015 vs database-limit threshold 0.9), and error_count is 0 in every window at a constant 60 rps (target and achieved). No material anomalies were reported (episodes_reported 0, anomalies_tested 4). Correlation analysis is not confirmatory: three CANDIDATE associations (cpu-queue, downstream-wait, generator-threads), two BELOW_EFFECT (system-cpu-work, system-db-work), three INSUFFICIENT_DATA, all headline selections UNAVAILABLE, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and clock alignment not verified by core. Advice: verify time bases first, locate the ~227ms tail population (p50 50ms, p99/max 248ms), investigate the downstream dependency and CPU-quota state, and re-run with load variation before attributing cause.

hypotheses.observation: In both windows response_time_p95_ms is 227 (lag threshold 200, operator lte) and both window-policy summaries report verdict FAIL with resource_verdict PASS; overall metrics show p50 50ms, p99 248ms, max 248ms, and error_count 0. The downstream-wait series (in_flight_requests) has a non-zero mean of ~2.28 in both windows, and association-08 (downstream-wait vs p95) is CANDIDATE with best_lag_ms 4000, best_lag_rho 0.6569, and partial_rho -0.4730.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A 227ms p95 with a 50ms p50 suggests a subset of requests experiences much higher latency. Because local CPU and database work are low and error_count is 0, the tail may come from time spent on the downstream dependency, the only non-zero in-flight series in the evidence; this is a hypothesis, not a proven cause, and the CANDIDATE correlation is not significance-tested.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment first (resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core); then inspect per-sample JTL latencies above ~200ms together with downstream dependency call start/duration (or add tracing) to see whether the tail coincides with dependency waits.

hypotheses.observation: cpu-service-quota quota_fraction is constant 1.0 in the reference and workload-01 windows; cpu-queue queue_depth mean is ~1.28 (median 1.37) with no missing cells; system-cpu-work is ~0.15 and the compute-limit policy check (system-cpu-work > 0.9) is PASS in both windows. Association-04 (cpu-queue vs p95) is CANDIDATE with best_lag_ms 2000, best_lag_rho 0.5879, and partial_rho 0.1660.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: At 100% of its CPU quota with a small non-zero queue (~1.3 requests), the service could be throttling requests even though whole-system CPU work is low (0.15 ratio); per-request queueing could push the p95 tail to 227ms while p50 stays at 50ms. The association is only CANDIDATE with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Check container/replica CPU throttle and quota counters around the latency tail; then run a controlled A/B comparison with an increased CPU quota at the same 60 rps and re-check response_time_p95_ms.

hypotheses.observation: Generator target_request_rate and request_starts are constant 60 requests/s in both windows; service worker_count is constant 4; response_time_p95_ms is identical (227) in both windows; associations of system-cpu-work and system-db-work with p95 are BELOW_EFFECT with reasons CONSTANT_CONTROL and RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM; anomaly checks report episodes_reported 0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The flat 60 rps load and constant resource/latency series mean the analysis cannot attribute the p95 value to load variation; the sustained 227ms p95 may be a structural baseline of the transaction or environment, but the evidence does not establish which component produces it.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Re-run with a stepped or ramped load (and/or a mixed request mix) so latency and resource series have variation, then re-run correlation and headline significance tests (currently UNAVAILABLE) to see whether p95 moves with load.

hypotheses.observation: generator active_threads has dips (min 2.950001, mean ~4.81 in reference; min 4.251333 and mean ~4.82 in workload-01) while request_starts stays at exactly 60 rps with error_count 0; association-09 (generator-threads vs p95) is CANDIDATE with best_lag_ms 3000, best_lag_rho 0.5839, and raw_rho 0.1210.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Generator thread-pool dips could alter request timing or burstiness and coincide with p95 spikes; since error_count is 0 and the generator is not the service under test, this is a lower-priority hypothesis and no causal claim is warranted.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect raw JTL sample timestamps around the thread-count dips for gaps or bursts, verify the generator clock, and check whether samples above 200ms cluster at those times.

hypotheses.observation: runtime-heap used_bytes mean is ~98.7MB (98,725,527.79 bytes) with slope_per_second +670.84 bytes/s in the reference window; service worker_count is constant 4; no GC metrics are present in the evidence.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Allocation pressure or garbage-collection pauses could add to tail latency even at low CPU utilization, but this is speculative because no GC or JVM pause evidence is present in the input.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect GC pause and JVM memory metrics over the same windows and check whether tail samples coincide with GC events; also trend heap over a longer run to see whether the +670.84 bytes/s slope persists.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment across the load generator, service, and telemetry before interpreting any lag-based correlation.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core; the candidate associations rely on best_lag_ms of 1000-4000ms and an unverified clock relationship cannot support lead/lag ordering or a temporal causal hypothesis.

recommendations.action: Disaggregate the tail: pull the raw JTL samples above ~200ms (or latency histograms) and examine them by time, thread, request label, and phase.
recommendations.rationale: The deterministic failure is tail latency - p95 227ms vs 200ms threshold with p50 50ms and p99/max 248ms - and aggregate percentiles alone cannot identify which requests form the tail.

recommendations.action: Instrument the downstream dependency: measure per-call duration and concurrency, and compare it with the latency sample distribution.
recommendations.rationale: downstream-wait in_flight is the only non-zero in-flight series (mean ~2.28) and its association (association-08) is CANDIDATE; dependency latency could explain the ~177ms gap between p50 (50ms) and p95 (227ms), but this needs direct per-call measurement.

recommendations.action: Check for CPU-quota throttling of service replicas and run a controlled quota A/B if throttling is observed.
recommendations.rationale: quota_fraction is constant 1.0 (100% of quota) while cpu-queue is ~1.28-1.37 and association-04 is CANDIDATE; although system-cpu-work is low (0.15) and the compute-limit check PASSes, quota-throttle delays could still contribute to the tail.

recommendations.action: Re-run with load variation (ramp/step or mixed request mix) and sufficient samples per window, then re-run correlation and significance tests.
recommendations.rationale: This run is constant-rate with constant resource series; CONSTANT_CONTROL / RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM caused BELOW_EFFECT and INSUFFICIENT_DATA pairs, and headline significances are UNAVAILABLE with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, so the current CANDIDATE associations are unverified.

recommendations.action: After any remediation, re-run the exact same windows and confirm response_time_p95_ms <= 200 (latency rule) in both windows while keeping the resource checks PASS.
recommendations.rationale: The deterministic verdict is FAIL solely from the latency rule in both windows (findings reference the two latency policy failures); remediation must be validated against that exact rule, and this advice never changes the verdict.

caveats: The deterministic verdict is FAIL (latency rule) in both windows; resource verdicts are PASS. This advisory does not alter that verdict.
Clock alignment is not verified by core; best_lag_ms values (1000-4000ms) in the candidate associations cannot support lead/lag ordering or temporal causality until clocks are verified.

All correlation headline selections are UNAVAILABLE (OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED or PAIR_NOT_EVALUABLE), uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED, and there are no p-values or Holm-adjusted p-values; CANDIDATE status does not imply a confirmed or statistically significant association.

Several series had no rank variation (admission-queue, db-queue, cpu-service-quota -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA) and system-cpu-work/system-db-work were BELOW_EFFECT (CONSTANT_CONTROL, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM), so no resource-effect claims are supported for them.

error_count 0, episodes_reported 0, anomalies_tested 4, and suppressed_short_episodes 30 do not prove stability, spare capacity, or absence of a latency problem; ZERO_MAD references limit dispersion-based detection and missing checks or findings do not constitute proof of absence.

The evidence is aggregate: window-level latency percentiles and resource summaries only; no per-sample JTL records, traces, or GC metrics are present, so the tail population and any dependency or GC attribution are unverified.
The test ran at a constant 60 rps with a constant target rate, so the analysis could not observe behavior under load variation; results may not generalize to other request rates.
Coverage limits: 8 family hypotheses, pairs_tested 8, pairs_evaluable 5, anomalies_tested 4; analysis_coverage status COMPLETE refers to processing completion, not proof of system correctness.
